Lastly I am not at all easy about the biggest genera & their varieties: could you spare once again & for short time, vols. 10, 11. & 12 with

: Labiat: & Acanthaceæ: I know I am unreasonable in this to give trouble of packing up & loss of use; but I cannot be easy without trying the sections. Yet if really inconvenient to spare them, I know you will say so, as that wd. be far pleasantest to me: if you do send them, send by enclosed address.—
I was not much struck with the great Buckle & I admired the way you stuck up about deduction & induction.— I heard that the other day that he met
for first time in party, & fairly silenced the old man with his harangues! I am reading his Book, which with much sophistry as it seems to me, is
tomba of Beethoven thoroughily; there is something grand in her sweet tones. My Brother, by the way, simply thinks Buckle the most infernal bore he ever met!
Farewell, I have partly written this note to drive
-cells out of my head; for I am half mad on subject to try to make out some simple steps from which all the wondrous angles may result.—
I was very glad to see Mrs.
; how well she appears to be & looks.
Forgive your intolerable but affectionate friend |
